What this answers

How the whole business stacks up — revenue → COGS → gross profit → opex → financing, by fiscal year.

How to read it

ARMCL has no SKU-level COGS in the ERP, so margin is reported at business-unit level from the GL journal (the honest, finance-consistent view). GP% is the key metric; financing cost is the largest drag on the bottom line.

Basis: Revenue = Sales Local + Foreign + Wastage (GL 3010001/2/3, net of returns). COGS = GL 4810001. GP% = (revenue − COGS) ÷ revenue. NP% = GP% less selling, logistics, marketing, admin, financing and depreciation. Other income (GL 3010004) shown separately.

What this answers

What ARMCL has declared for each SKU — the DP / TP / MRP price ladder — and coverage gaps.

How to read it

DP = Distributor price (channel 71), TP = Trade/Dealer price (channel 70), MRP = retail list price. This three-level ladder is ARMCL's price architecture. Realised trade-net should sit between TP and DP — a SKU trading >5% below TP is a discount leak.

Declared price ladder coverage

SKUs with a declared DP, TP and MRP. The gap between DP coverage and MRP coverage is the price-architecture gap.

Price-architecture notes (from the ARMCL price cockpit)

What this answers

How strongly volume responds to price, grade by grade.

What β means

β is own-price elasticity — the % change in volume for a 1% change in price. β = −2: a 10% price rise → ~20% volume drop. β > 0: price and volume move together (often cost pass-through or project cycles for ready-mix, not demand).

How to read it

Volume is derived (revenue ÷ blended price) and prices are mixed-grade, so β is directional, not a causal demand curve. Ready-mix is project-driven: volume follows the construction pipeline more than price, so most grades read not-measurable or anomalous.

Elasticity by category (β = Δln volume ÷ Δln price) — Jul'24 → Oct'26

First-difference estimator over consecutive months. Teal = β<0 (normal). Red = β>0 (anomalous / supply-driven).

Price vs volume, within category — Jul'24 → Oct'26

Each point = one category-month; ln(price) and ln(volume) demeaned to the category's own mean. Colour = sign of that category's β.

Elasticity table

Read with care. Volume is derived (revenue ÷ blended price), prices are mixed-grade, and ready-mix demand is project/season-driven. Treat β as a signal to investigate, not a causal demand curve.

What this answers

How ARMCL sells — the channel mix — and where trade incentives sit.

How to read it

ARMCL is B2B corporate-first: nearly all revenue is Corporate Sales (direct to construction projects / developers), with a small Asphalt (road-surfacing) line. There is no dealer/retail network or distributor tier, so there is no dealer-commission table in this ERP (the arl_erp commission source was empty at build time). Trade levers are booked discounts and free goods.

Method

  • Revenue = numNetValue (orders), ৳ Cr. Deficit revenue uses the GL journal (net of returns) to match the flash-report metric.
  • Category = keyword classifier on strItemName (ready-mix concrete by PSI grade — PCC vs OPC, −D/−R/−G/−N variants — plus Asphalt and Wastage lines).
  • Realised net price = revenue ÷ quantity (blended across PSI grades — directional only).
  • GP% = (revenue − COGS) ÷ revenue, GL-level. Break-even gross margin ≈ 13.5% of revenue.
  • Elasticity β = OLS slope of Δln(volume) on Δln(price); gated at ≥8 pairs, |β| ≤ 5, R² ≥ 0.10, price dispersion ≥ 2%.
  • Price moves = |Δ| ≥ 20% MoM with ratio guard 0.5–2.
  • Fiscal year = July–June; label = start year (FY2026-27 = "2026").
  • GL map: revenue 3010001/2/3 · COGS 4810001 · manufacturing 4010001 · selling 4310001 · logistics 4410001 · marketing 4210001 · admin 4110001 · financial 4510001 · depreciation 4610001 · other income 3010004 (excluded from revenue).
  • No SKU-level COGS — per-SKU margin / a true loss-making list is not published; the price-realisation screen is used instead.
